topic.title: The block button as breakup ritual
topic.claim: We don't break up anymore, we block and unblock, and the Instagram password has become the new test of love.
topic.behaviour: Couples block each other everywhere after a fight, reappear weeks later, and treat access to each other's accounts as proof of trust.
topic.mechanism: Online access feels like intimacy, so removing it feels like punishment and restoring it feels like forgiveness. It keeps people in limbo instead of letting them end things.
topic.group: Gen Z and young millennials in relationships
real_details: A long-distance relationship nearly 3 years old broke down after a big fight in January 2026
She blocked him on every platform
He later blocked her Instagram and then unblocked it a month on, asking forgiveness
She asked for his Instagram password and he refused
Both stopped messaging after he started ignoring her
topic.why_now: The thread is a clear example of the block, unblock and password pattern.

score.reason: Fresh, specific Gen Z relationship ritual with real emotional pull
score.best_hook: We don't break up anymore. We block, we unblock, and we hand back the Instagram password like it's a peace treaty.
